summary: The Banach NAWA programme is run by the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange together with the Polish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, as part of Poland's development cooperation. It gives scholarships to citizens of 36 listed countries for full-time second-cycle (master's) studies in Poland, in Polish or English, or for a one-year Polish preparatory course before studies in Polish. The scholarship pays PLN 2,500 a month, exempts fees at public universities and NAWA preparatory courses, and pays a one-off travel lump sum. The details below come from the 2026/27 call; no 2027/28 call was published when checked.
eligibility_notes:
Country: you must be a citizen of one of 36 programme countries: Albania, Angola, Argentina, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil, Georgia, India, Indonesia, Iraq, Iran, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Kosovo, Lebanon, Mexico, Moldova, Mongolia, Montenegro, Nigeria, North Macedonia, Palestine, Papua New Guinea, Peru, Philippines, Rwanda, Senegal, Serbia, Tanzania, Tunisia, Ukraine, Uzbekistan, Vietnam. In the application system these are sorted into four groups by citizenship.

Citizenship: you must not hold Polish citizenship and must not have applied for it.

Degree: you must have a first-cycle (bachelor's) degree from a programme country obtained no earlier than 2024, or be in the final semester of first-cycle studies in a programme country and obtain the degree by 15 July 2026 (2026/27 call). The information page adds that applicants with a bachelor's degree from Poland are not eligible. You must not already hold a second-cycle or uniform master's degree (where the country has no two-cycle system, holders of a master's or equivalent may apply), and must never have received a NAWA Director's scholarship for second-cycle studies.

Start: you must plan to start second-cycle studies or a preparatory course in the winter semester (from October 2026 in the last call). Studies starting in February are not covered.

Language: B2 Polish to start studies in Polish; B2 English to start studies in English; B1 Polish for the preparatory course path. Proof of at least B2 in the language of instruction is also needed in the university's own admission.

You may submit only one application. The scholarship path you choose in the application is binding for the whole time in the programme.
age_experience_notes: No age limit and no work experience requirement are stated. The bachelor's degree must be dated 2024 or later (2026/27 call) or be completed by 15 July 2026.
funding_summary: The scholarship pays PLN 2,500 a month during the regular education period, for at most 12 months in an academic year (at most 5 months in the winter semester and 7 in the summer semester), starting with the first month of classes or of the preparatory course. Fees are waived at NAWA preparatory courses and at public universities; at private universities the fees are set by the university and arranged individually. A one-off lump sum for the trip to Poland is paid with the first monthly payment. The call does not state the amount of the lump sum or the total length of funding for the master's.
programmes_note: Full-time second-cycle (master's) studies in Polish or English, in any field the applicant picks from the offers of eligible universities; the call sets no list of fields. Two paths: a Polish-language path, either a one-year NAWA preparatory course followed by studies in Polish or studies in Polish without the course; or an English path with studies in English plus a Polish language and culture course in September and October before studies. Study programmes are found through the Polish government study portals (a Polish-language one and an English study finder).
institutions_note: Eligible hosts are universities supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education that have a framework agreement with NAWA: 113 entries in the 2026/27 list, including University of Warsaw, Jagiellonian University in Krakow, Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznan, AGH University of Krakow, Warsaw University of Technology, Wroclaw University of Science and Technology, Gdansk University of Technology, SGH Warsaw School of Economics, Nicolaus Copernicus University in Torun, University of Wroclaw, Lodz University of Technology, Poznan University of Life Sciences and Warsaw University of Life Sciences. NAWA does not handle admission: you apply to the university yourself, separately from the scholarship application. For the preparatory course, NAWA assigns a centre, depending on your planned field and free places.

summary.detail: Full-time second-cycle studies in Polish or English at universities with a NAWA framework agreement. Any field the applicant selects. Fees are waived at public universities. PLN 2,500 a month. B2 in the language of instruction is needed for university admission. Studies must start in the winter semester (October in the last call). The length of the master's is not stated in the call.

One-year NAWA preparatory course on scholarship terms, before second-cycle studies in Polish. It deepens Polish and teaches subjects related to the planned field. Entry needs Polish at B1. Applicants on this path join the university admission for the following academic year while attending the course; no proof of university admission is needed at application. Scholarship holders on the English path instead take a Polish language and culture course in September and October.
summary.source_text: NAWA preparatory course preceding studies in Poland

benefits.limit_text: PLN 2,500 per month, for at most 12 months in an academic year (at most 5 in the winter semester, 7 in the summer semester)
benefits.conditions: Paid from the first month of classes or of the preparatory course. Holders on-site for the Polish language and culture course before studies get the first payment from September 2026 (2026/27 call). Paid through the university or the preparatory-course unit.

benefits.limit_text: Exemption from fees at NAWA preparatory courses and at public universities
benefits.conditions: At private universities the fees are decided by the university and must be agreed individually between the holder and the university.

benefits.limit_text: One-off lump sum for international travel to Poland
benefits.conditions: Paid once together with the first monthly payment of PLN 2,500. The amount is not stated in the call.

benefits.limit_text: No separate accommodation payment is mentioned
benefits.conditions: The call lists only the monthly scholarship, fee exemption and travel lump sum.
The call and the information page read do not mention insurance.

requirements.text: Page of a passport (a document allowing border crossing) with your personal data. Scans of originals or documents with a qualified electronic signature.

First-cycle diploma from a programme country, with the supplement showing the average of grades for the whole course and grades for completed subjects. If the average is missing, NAWA works it out from the grade shown.

Final-semester students or those without the diploma yet send a scanned university certificate showing: name, university, programme, completion date (actual or planned), average grade with all completed subjects and final grades, and the university stamp. A sample is attached to the call.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only if you have no first-cycle diploma yet

requirements.text: Proof of taking part in admission to full-time second-cycle studies starting in the winter semester at a Polish university with a NAWA framework agreement: an admission decision (also conditional), a promise or letter of acceptance (also preliminary), confirmation of taking part in admission (for example registration email, admission account or paid admission fee, naming the field), or proof of contact with the university about a named field together with its reply. It must identify you (name, email or passport data).
requirements.conditional_rule: Not required on the Polish-language path with a preparatory course

requirements.text: Proof of the language you will study in: a certificate from the call's lists of recognised Polish or English certificates (for English at B2, for example IELTS Academic 5.5, TOEFL iBT 72, PTE Academic 59, Cambridge B2 First or higher). For the preparatory course path: Polish at B1 by a language certificate, a secondary school or first-cycle diploma taught in Polish, or a certificate of completing a Polish course.
Video self-presentation of 1 to 3 minutes in Polish or English, explaining your choice of field and your motivation to study in Poland. No images of other people.
Letter of recommendation from a Polish diplomatic or consular mission for your area. Optional, but it can add up to 10 points.

Translation into Polish or English of any attachment in another language, certified by a sworn translator's signature and stamp or by a Polish diplomatic or consular mission. Where there are no sworn translators, a notary translator, an ordinary translator or a Polish teacher (certified by the school stamp) is accepted.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only for documents not in Polish or English

application_steps.title: Choose your path and check eligibility
application_steps.detail: Check that you are a citizen of a programme country, meet the degree and date rules, and choose one path: Polish language with a preparatory course, studies in Polish, or studies in English. The path is binding. Check the university's admission rules, including proof of B2.

application_steps.title: Apply to a Polish university yourself
application_steps.detail: NAWA does not take part in admissions. For studies paths, register in the university's online admission system by its deadline and keep proof of admission, registration or contact, which the scholarship application requires. The university may also ask for legalised or apostilled documents or confirmation that your diploma allows second-cycle admission.

application_steps.title: Submit one application in the NAWA online system
application_steps.detail: In the NAWA IT system, choose the group for your citizenship, fill in the form in Polish or English and attach the documents, including the 1-3 minute video. Only one application is allowed. In the 2026/27 call the deadline was 8 May 2026, 3 p.m. Warsaw time, and a group closed early once 300 applications (groups 1-3) or 200 (group 4) came in. An incomplete application may be returned once for completion within 14 days.

application_steps.title: Formal check of the application
application_steps.detail: NAWA first checks that the application meets the formal criteria of the call.

application_steps.title: Scoring of the application
application_steps.detail: Maximum 110 points: 0-70 for the average grade of first-cycle studies (average x 70 / top of the grading scale), 0-30 for the self-presentation video (goals, reasons for the field and Poland, expected impact), and 0-10 for the recommendation of a Polish mission. A positive result needs at least 70 points, with at least 50 in the first criterion and 20 in the second; below 50 in the first, the video is not scored.

application_steps.title: Awards within country quotas and results
application_steps.detail: Scholarships go to the highest scorers within limits set for each country, which depend on the share of correct applications by citizenship and on Poland's foreign policy and development goals; unused places are redistributed. Results were announced by 31 July 2026 on the NAWA site and sent through the application system.

application_steps.title: Complete university admission and send proof
application_steps.detail: Finish the admission formalities at your chosen university and submit the admission certificate through the NAWA system. Preparatory-course students are assigned a centre by NAWA and enter university admission for the following year during the course.

application_steps.title: Sign the scholarship agreement within 45 days
application_steps.detail: Conclude the scholarship agreement under the programme no later than 45 days from the date it is made available in the NAWA system. Your contact data are shared with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

application_steps.title: Start studies or the course and report yearly
application_steps.detail: Begin the preparatory course or second-cycle studies in the winter semester; English-path holders do a Polish language and culture course first, in September and October (on-site or online). Submit an annual report by 31 October after each academic year; the first one is due after the preparatory course, or after the first year of studies for holders without a course.
